Earlier this week, a lost note led an experienced planner to ask questions. Incident Report: Misrouted Companion Animal File at Aurelia Skyways. The matter began in the welcome area, where a traveler arrived with a carrier and a nervous pet and reported that a crate entry had gone missing from the handoff stack. The senior coordinator checked the intake board, then reviewed the desk log and the carrier tag against the boarding list. The traveler said the animal had been calm during check-in, but became uneasy after a delay in the transfer line, and the companion animal staff took the report as a service concern rather than a security event.

A search of the nearby work area found the misplaced note under a clipboard, which explained why the file had not reached the outbound desk. The supervisor listened carefully to the traveler and confirmed that the pet remained safe and under control. <<FACT F118>> The records aide then copied the relevant details into the incident file and marked the crate as recovered in the local log.

During the review, the traveler also mentioned a minor scrape to a hand while steadying the carrier. <<FACT F113>> The desk advised the traveler on the normal service path for follow-up and noted that the report would be routed through the usual handling channel. No extra transport was needed, and the pet was later accepted for the flight without further concern.

The follow-up steps were straightforward. The welcome team was reminded to keep paper notes clipped to the active file before transfer, and the senior coordinator asked for a clearer sweep of the counter before each boarding call. The traveler left satisfied that the matter had been heard and that the record now matched the crate. The Companion Animal Travel Desk will keep this report on file and continue checking handoff papers more closely.
